BBC News (Dan Sales) — published Thursday 24 September 2026 18:28 BST (cXenseParse:publishtime 2026-09-24T17:28:31Z UTC), updated 20:16 BST

HEADLINE: 'It has broken us as a family,' mother of poison seller victim tells hearing

FACTS:
- This is the SECOND day of a FOUR-DAY sentencing hearing of Kenneth Law in Ontario, Canada. The hearing continues (so it runs into Friday 25 and Monday).
- Law, a Canadian former chef, has admitted 14 counts of aiding suicide in Canada. British authorities have confirmed 79 UK victims also died after using his products.
- A plea deal with Canadian authorities means Law will NOT face charges in the UK or over any British deaths, but impact statements from British families are being read this week.
- Authorities say Law sold about 1,200 packages of toxic substances to recipients from 40 different countries he met in online suicide forums. Roughly a quarter of the packages were sent to the UK.
- He was arrested in May 2023 following an investigation by at least 11 law-enforcement agencies involving investigators from around a dozen countries, including the UK, Italy and the US.
- Samuel Whitaker, a University of Warwick student, was 19 and was found collapsed outside his halls after taking poison sold by Law.
- Other British victims named at the hearing: Danielle Cornish; Faith Ike-Elechi; Michael Dunham; Yeanu Mistry; Gary Cooper; Aimee Louise Elif Walton from Southampton.

QUOTE (Tanya Whitaker, mother of Samuel Whitaker, to the Canadian court on Thursday): "He barely had a chance."
QUOTE (Tanya Whitaker): "The enormity of losing a child is catastrophic. Samuel was just 19 when he was handed the tools that ended his precious life."
QUOTE (Tanya Whitaker): "It has broken me completely and utterly. It has broken us as a family and me as a mother. Our son died alone at university 100 miles away from his family. We will never be able to forgive ourselves for this happening."
QUOTE (Tanya Whitaker, of her husband Paul): "He is a shell of himself today. Broken and devastated beyond repair."
QUOTE (Debbie Cornish, mother of Danielle Cornish, written statement): "Words on paper can't even begin to describe the painful loss of our amazing daughter. Nothing will be the same ever again as we are part of a surreal nightmare. Nearly four years on, we are still fighting to keep our family together... not to mention the constant thoughts of how she may have died."
QUOTE (Debbie Cornish): "KL has changed the life of many many families all across the world as well as ours. We are living a constant nightmare."
QUOTE (Maurice Dunham, father of Michael Dunham, written statement): "The last conversation I had with him was an argument." ... "The feeling I had was like an electric shock going through me. I blamed myself for not stopping Michael from leaving the hotel room. I planned to take my own life. I didn't care if I lived or died."
QUOTE (Adele Zeynep Walton, sister of Aimee Walton, video statement): "She died in a strange place, in a strange city, in the company of a stranger. You only need to listen to the recording of the emergency call to know how much she suffered during the last moments of her life."
QUOTE (Maureen Cooper, mother of Gary Cooper, written statement): "A death such as this is the thing of nightmares."
QUOTE (Elisabeth Belien, British survivor, who told the court on Wednesday): "I feel guilty for surviving. Although I survived, it has also impacted my loved ones. I feel like my vulnerability was exploited. I still feel a lot of shame about what happened."
